links.outcome: Discrimination and calibration of CRASH model on local retrospective data against observed 14-day mortality
links.effect: AuROC 0.92 (Basic) and 0.93 (CT); calibration-in-the-large -0.916 and -1.257, slopes 1.69 and 1.86, showing overestimation of mortality locally.
links.quote: However, calibration metrics indicated a systematic overestimation of mortality, suggesting that recalibration of both the intercept and slope is necessary before the model can be implemented in local clinical practice.

links.outcome: Effect of logistic recalibration of intercept and slope on calibration in local population
links.effect: Recalibration reduced overestimation in high-risk groups and better aligned predictions with observed mortality (shown in plots; no numeric post-recalibration metrics in text).
links.quote: The recalibration process effectively reduced this overestimation, aligning predicted outcomes with observed mortality rates.

links.outcome: Differences between development and local validation populations (age, GCS, CT findings, mortality)
links.effect: 75% aged ≥55 vs 14.5% in development; mortality 9.1% vs 20.7%; non-evacuated hematoma 62.1% vs 27.3%; miscalibration followed.
links.quote: Patients in the validation dataset were predominantly older, with 75% aged 55 or above, compared to only 14.5% in the development cohort (STD = 1.940).

links.outcome: Generalization of CRASH model to new population (TBI with ICH in Thai ED)
links.effect: Discrimination retained (AuROC 0.92/0.93) but systematic overestimation of mortality (CITL -0.916 Basic, -1.257 CT).
links.quote: These results suggest that the models systematically predict higher risks of 14-day mortality than observed, particularly in higher-risk groups.
However, calibration metrics in this study indicated a significant overestimation of mortality risk, as evidenced by a negative calibration-in-the-large.

links.effect: CT AuROC 0.93 (95% CI: 0.86–0.99) versus Basic 0.92; no statistical difference (P-value=0.679).
links.quote: The CT model also demonstrated outstanding discriminative performance in the validation dataset, with an AuROC of 0.93 (95% CI: 0.86–0.99), slightly higher than the Basic model with no statistical difference ( P -value=0.679).

links.effect: Local validation found high discrimination (Basic AuROC 0.92; CT 0.93) but miscalibration/overestimation: Basic CITL -0.916, slope 1.69; CT CITL -1.257, slope 1.86.
links.quote: However, calibration metrics indicated a systematic overestimation of mortality, suggesting that recalibration of both the intercept and slope is necessary before the model can be implemented in local clinical practice.

links.effect: Age ≥55: 75.0% versus 14.5% (STD=1.940); mortality at 14 days: 9.1% versus 20.7% (STD=0.332).

links.effect: After original miscalibration (Basic CITL −0.916, slope 1.69; CT CITL −1.257, slope 1.86), recalibration reduced overestimation.
links.quote: The recalibration process effectively reduced this overestimation, aligning predicted outcomes with observed mortality rates.

links.effect: Basic model had AuROC 0.92 (95% CI: 0.84, 1.00) and CT model 0.93 (95% CI: 0.86, 1.00), but both had significant miscalibration (Basic CITL -0.916; CT CITL -1.257).
links.quote: The original CRASH prediction model demonstrates strong discriminative ability for predicting 14-day mortality in TBI patients; however, significant miscalibration was observed.
